pattern-selector.why: the engine is a deliberate record-plus-gate split: a small Stop hook reads a task record and checks six groups, rather than re-deriving each proof (a fresh-context review, coverage) inside the hook; the forces (turn-boundary latency, non-reproducible proofs) and the rejected re-derive option are named in ADR-0100.
pattern-selector.what: added always-on/finish-check.mjs as a thin reader-over-record checker; recorded the pattern choice and its alternatives in ADR-0100.
quotes: the structure that fits the forces this system will actually face, chosen on purpose

architectural-decision-records.why: the finish-check is a significant new enforcement mechanism; the decision, its fail-closed contract, the PR-A/PR-B scope split, and the rejected alternatives are recorded in the same change.
architectural-decision-records.what: wrote ADR-0100 (the finish-check: a fail-closed Stop hook).
quotes: Every architecturally significant change ships with an ADR in the same unit of work

bdd-comprehensive-testing.why: the enforcement behavior is specified as executable scenarios across audiences (agent, subagent, operator) and happy/negative/concurrency/timeout/adverse paths, tagged, logged, and reconciled against the committed datastore.
bdd-comprehensive-testing.what: added 21 scenarios to the two always-on feature files and a step file that drives the real finish-check.mjs; regenerated the datastore and appended the coverage-log receipt; the full chain (gherkin-valid, tags, coverage, bdd-run, check-bdd-executed) is green at 73 scenarios.
quotes: These are not optional and not left to judgment.

comprehensive-test-strategy.why: the engine is proven at the lowest level that can catch the bug: unit tests that spawn the real engine with crafted records and payloads, not a UI or integration run.
comprehensive-test-strategy.what: added test/finish-check.test.mjs (17 discriminating tests) and wired it into the package.json test list.
quotes: Test at the lowest level that can catch the bug

verifiable-quality-gates.why: the finish-check is itself a quality gate, so each of its block branches carries a test that fails when the engine is replaced by a no-op (always exit 0); the gate fails closed on every error path.
verifiable-quality-gates.what: wrote discriminating tests that flip when finish-check.mjs is neutralized, and made every error path in finish-check.mjs route to block (exit 2).
quotes: test must FAIL when the check is replaced by a no-op

skeptical-audit.why: the ADR and the record-format doc state the honest limit (the gate proves the record is present, complete and consistent, not that the work is true or good) and name the fail-open corner in the transcript derivation, rather than overclaiming the guarantee.
skeptical-audit.what: documented the evidence limits and the known fail-open corner in ADR-0100 and finish-check-records.md.
quotes: If you cannot attach all three, you do not assert it

judge-arch.why: a fresh-context review of the whole change was dispatched to a subagent against the four questions and recorded in the append-only review log before the PR.
judge-arch.what: ran judge-arch in fresh context, resolved its findings, and appended the review entry.
quotes: These are not optional and not left to discretion. Every review does all of them.

release-deployment-safety.why: the engine ships dormant: with ESK_TASK_RECORD unset it is a no-op notice, so landing the file cannot break any machine, and the installer (PR-B) is what turns it on - deploy kept apart from release.
release-deployment-safety.what: made the engine inert until wired, and documented the not-wired escape in ADR-0100 and finish-check-records.md.
quotes: Dark-launch: ship the code off, turn it on for internal users, then 1 percent

enterprise-architecture-standards.why: the engine is kept to one responsibility (read a record, check six groups, fail closed) rather than a larger re-derive-everything design; the simpler shape that meets the requirement was chosen on purpose.
enterprise-architecture-standards.what: built a single-responsibility checker with a documented contract, declining the larger alternative in ADR-0100.
quotes: Simplicity that meets the real requirement is a core principle, not a shortcut.

owasp-secure-coding-bdd.why: the engine's inputs are the trusted Claude Code Stop payload and installer-set ESK_ configuration, not an external attack surface; its malformed-input handling is treated as reliability (fail closed) and is covered by the malformed-payload and crash tests, not as a new security control, so no @security scenario is owed here.

compliance-data-lifecycle.why: the finish-check stores no personal or regulated data; it derives file paths from the transcript and discards them, and writes only a small block counter, so there is no data class, retention, or deletion duty in this change.

sre-operational-readiness.why: this adds no running service or endpoint; the loop-safety escalate-after-cap behavior is operational resilience but is covered by the finish-check reliability tests, not by SLIs/alerts/runbooks.

arch-encode.why: no greppable mistake was caught that needs a new arch-gate forbid rule in this change; the enforcement here is a runtime hook plus discriminating tests, not a static rule.

universal-accessibility-wcag.why: no user interface; the only human-facing output is plain-text operator messages on stderr.

universal-browser-device-support.why: no browser or device surface; this is a Node Stop hook.

usability-ux-universal-design.why: no end-user UI; the block and escalate messages are written in plain language naming the missing item and its fix, but there is no interactive surface to design.
